Verified unreachable, two ways:

- Every test overrides the seam (autoupdate_test.go:31, versioncheck_test.go:730), so realRunInstaller isn't called in tests either. The goos == goosWindows branch has zero coverage and no caller on any platform.

But the more interesting part is that the branch wouldn't work if it were reached, so it's not the safety net it claims to be. Look at what UpdateCommandForCurrentBinary actually returns on Windows, run through cmd /C:

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                       Command                       │                                       Through cmd.exe                                       │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ irm …install.ps1 -UseBasicParsing | iex             │ breaks — cmd treats | as its own pipe, and irm/iex are PowerShell cmdlets, not cmd commands │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ & ([scriptblock]::Create((irm …))) -Channel nightly │ breaks — leading & is a cmd command separator; syntax error                                 │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ cmd.exe /D /C "scoop install … && …"                │ works, but double-nested cmd /C cmd /C                                                      │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ mise upgrade entire                                 │ works                                                                                       │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Whoever lifts Windows print-only needs powershell -NoProfile -Command (or, better, the in-process rename-and-replace from the research above, no shell at all). # Plan: per-OS install detection + relocated install roots for `UpdateCommandForCurrentBinary`

Repo: `github.com/entireio/cli` (Go 1.26, cobra). Package: `cmd/entire/cli/versioncheck/`.
Base branch: `feat/windows-ps1-autoupdate` (commit `f1f8b24be` plus its uncommitted work — commit or land that first; do not build on a dirty tree).
Work in a fresh git worktree + branch. Read `CLAUDE.md` first; run `mise run fmt && mise run lint` (if `mise run lint` fails on a stale golangci-lint v1, run the mise-installed v2 binary directly: `~/.local/share/mise/installs/golangci-lint/2.11.3/golangci-lint-2.11.3-darwin-arm64/golangci-lint run ./cmd/entire/cli/versioncheck/...`) and `go test ./cmd/entire/cli/versioncheck/` before every commit.

Deliver as **two stacked PRs** (A then B). Do not merge the concerns.

---

## Background the code must respect (all verified against sources)

**What the function does.** `UpdateCommandForCurrentBinary(currentVersion string) string` (`versioncheck.go`, ~line 421) returns the shell one-liner that upgrades *this running binary*. It has 8 external call sites (`checkpoint_policy_write.go`, `checkpoint_policy_warning.go`, `hooks_git_cmd.go`, `hook_registry.go` x2, `strategy/checkpoint_policy.go`, plus `autoupdate.go`, `versioncheck.go`). **Signature must not change.** Several callers run inside git hooks → it must stay offline, no subprocesses, no package-manager queries.

**Current detection** (`installManagerForCurrentBinary`, ~line 389): resolve `os.Executable()` → `filepath.EvalSymlinks` → `filepath.ToSlash` (`normalizedExecPath`), then substring match:
- brew: `/Cellar/`, `/opt/homebrew/`, `/linuxbrew/`, `/Caskroom/`
- mise: `/mise/installs/`
- scoop: `/scoop/apps/`
- else: `if goos == goosWindows` → `install.ps1` one-liners (`windowsInstallCmd`, `windowsInstallNightlyCmd`), else `curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash` (± `-s -- --channel nightly`).
Order brew → mise → scoop. Nightly detection via `releaseChannel(currentVersion)`.

**`goos` is a runtime test seam** (`var goos = runtime.GOOS`, `versioncheck.go:27`). It is ALSO used by `autoupdate.go` (~line 76) for the Windows print-only gate in `maybeAutoUpdate`. **Keep the seam and that gate untouched.** Only the `goos` check inside `UpdateCommandForCurrentBinary` goes away.

**Platform facts:**
- **Scoop is Windows-only** (uses registry, `WindowsPrincipal`, `user32.dll`, Robocopy). `scoop install` has NO per-app path flag. Every app lands at `<root>\apps\<app>\<version>` with a `current` junction. Roots (from `lib/core.ps1`):
  - user: `$env:SCOOP` → config `root_path` → `%USERPROFILE%\scoop`
  - global (`scoop install -g`): `$env:SCOOP_GLOBAL` → config `global_path` → `%ProgramData%\scoop`
  - config file: `~/.config/scoop/config.json` (`XDG_CONFIG_HOME` honored) — confirm exact resolution in `ScoopInstaller/Scoop/lib/core.ps1` before implementing.
  - `PATH` holds `<root>\shims`, which contains a launcher `entire.exe` + `entire.shim` (`path = <root>\apps\entire\current\entire.exe`). The shim SPAWNS the real exe, so `os.Executable()` inside entire returns the `apps\...` path, never `shims\`. After `EvalSymlinks` the junction resolves, so the path may read `apps/entire/0.10.5/entire.exe` OR `apps/entire/current/entire.exe`. App name = first segment after `<root>/apps/`.
  - Scoop package was renamed `cli` → `entire`; `scoopAppName()=="cli"` returns a migration command. Keep that logic and its long comment; move it, don't rewrite it.
- **mise** runs on all three OSes → the ONLY shared manager. Installs at `$MISE_INSTALLS_DIR` → `$MISE_DATA_DIR/installs` → `${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/mise/installs`, layout `installs/<tool>/<version>`. Docs give no Windows default; do not hardcode one — the `/mise/installs/` marker covers defaults.
- **brew**: `entire` ships as a **cask** (`brew install --cask entire`, tap `entireio/tap`, `Casks/entire.rb` with `binary "entire"`, `binary "git-remote-entire"`), NOT a formula. Binary lives at `<prefix>/Caskroom/entire/<version>/entire`; `<prefix>/bin/entire` is a symlink to it → `EvalSymlinks` yields the Caskroom path. `brew install` has no per-formula/cask path option; Caskroom is always `<prefix>/Caskroom` (man page defines `brew --caskroom` that way, no documented override). Therefore the `/Caskroom/` marker is complete by construction: **brew needs NO env-var work.** `/Cellar/` describes a formula install that doesn't exist for entire.
- **Windows CI** (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, job `test-windows`) runs `go test ./cmd/entire/cli/... -run '(Windows|MSYS)'`. **Any `//go:build windows` test whose top-level name lacks `Windows` or `MSYS` never runs anywhere.** Non-Windows CI (`test-core`, ubuntu) runs the whole package.

### Target shape


Probe order preserves current precedence (brew→mise on unix, scoop→mise on windows).

Note on `/Cellar/`: entire is a cask, so this marker matches nothing we ship. Either drop it or keep it with a one-line comment that it is defensive for a hypothetical formula. Either way, change the test fixture `/opt/homebrew/Cellar/entire/1.0.0/bin/entire` to a Caskroom path (`/opt/homebrew/Caskroom/entire/1.0.0/entire`) so tests describe the real install.

- `versioncheck_unix_test.go` (`//go:build unix`): moved verbatim — brew stable (Caskroom path), brew via `/opt/homebrew/bin/entire`, brew nightly, linuxbrew, curl fallback stable, curl fallback nightly, exec-error → curl. ## PR B — honor relocated install roots (behavioral, stacked on A)

Only Scoop and mise change. Brew: nothing (see background).

| Probe | `roots()` returns (each normalized, see below) |
|---|---|
| mise (shared) | `$MISE_INSTALLS_DIR` if set; else `$MISE_DATA_DIR/installs` if set; else nil (marker covers defaults incl. `XDG_DATA_HOME` relocation) |

`matches(path)`: `true` if any root (with trailing `/`) is a prefix of `path`, OR any marker is a substring. `scoopAppName(execPath, matchedRoot string)`: app = first path segment after `<matchedRoot>/apps/` (or after `/scoop/apps/` when matched by marker). `command` receives the exec path; have `matches` return the matched root too, or re-derive — keep it simple, one helper.
